scope: Originally produced and locally installed Linux x86-64 Maven JARs/POMs, JDK 22.0.2, Lean 4.32.2, Kotlin 2.2.0, kotlinx-coroutines-core-jvm 1.8.0, Maven 3.9.11. glibc 2.36 override on this test host; normal release floor 2.38. No registry publication, hosted CI, or full-matrix promotion. Callback arguments and replies in this task profile are copied primitives, not nominal resource leases or asynchronous host functions.
checks: Ordinary and compiler-reviewed Feedback plus an independently built Relay: original archives, repository sidecars, every archived payload, native runtimes, Binding IR, Java classes, Kotlin metadata, resolved coroutines artifact and POM dependencies verified. Offline Maven resolution and relocation; client runtime PATH contains no tools. Repeated with both load orders in Java and Kotlin.

Real Lean workers and factories invoke standard Java functional interfaces and synchronous Kotlin functions from JVM virtual threads. All 19 copied scalar carriers; nested same-component and cross-component calls return normally, and attempting to join the active callback’s own future is rejected.

Preserve the original throwable when its Lean IO error escapes; observe Lean catches, equal-text replacement errors, typed factory errors and invalid boundary replies separately. Callback CancellationException is distinct from cancelling a Java future. A hostile exception formatter does not replace error identity on join, get or timed get; repeated timed waits do not retain a new dependent each time. Interruption and reading a subsequently obtruded value are also exercised.

Self-revocation lets the current call finish and rejects future calls, including in a different component. Cancelling one task leaves a shared registration usable. Cooperative/late cancellation, unentered requests, weakly observed capture release while the cancelled future remains reachable, expired Lean-side callback, cancellation while a lambda is blocked and retirement while a lambda is blocked. Kotlin uses its native cancellable suspend API; negative cases fail at compile time.

Two components, one runtime, zero native identities and no net eventfd/epoll descriptors after cleanup. Fatal JVM linkage error retires the shared runtime; a separate process verifies that a late fatal callback after cancellation still retires both packages without changing the already-cancelled future.

A new retained callback reenters the previously accepted synchronous Journal and async Timers packages. The three original-first permutations all observe one runtime, three attached components and zero remaining identities. A fresh offline-installed CLI reproduces the primary release byte for byte.
Changed reviewed scheduler and callback ownership/lifetime, and a non-scalar callback reply in Lean source, all fail without an exposed handoff.

regression.before: The original JVM get() constructed ExecutionException(Throwable); Throwable.toString invoked the user's broken formatter, masking the exception already preserved by join().
regression.after: A shared nonthrowing signal preserves interruption and timeout without retaining waiters; a fresh checked read uses ExecutionException(null, original).

reproduce: Set the JDK 22, Kotlin 2.2.0, Maven, Python >=3.11, and Lean 4.32.2 paths as for docs/evidence/jvm-tasks-20261123.json. Use an empty EVIDENCE directory, LEAN_NUM_THREADS=1, and the test glibc override only on a compatible test host. Seed LEAN_BRIDGE_JVM_TASK_M2_SEED with the third-party prerequisites from tests/fixtures/jvm-tasks/prerequisites.xml, never any application JAR.
LEAN_BRIDGE_JVM_ORIGINAL=$EVIDENCE LEAN_BRIDGE_JVM_REPRO=$SECOND node --test --test-name-pattern='offline-installed CLI in a second producer' tests/helpers/jvm-io-installed.mjs
